item.title: Valkyries-Dream WNBA Finals Game 6 will be played at 9:30 a.m. PT Thursday
item.description: Tiffany Hayes of the Golden State Valkyries shoots the ball past Allisha Gray of the Atlanta Dream during the fourth quarter in Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena on Oct. 24, 2026 in Atlanta. (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) On the day of Game 5 of the tied WNBA Finals, the Golden State Valkyries finally found out when and where they'll play Game 6 : in the middle of a workday morning for San Francisco fans. The WNBA brought an end to the chaotic few days of uncertainty by announcing Game 6 in Atlanta will be played at 12:30 p.m. Eastern/9:30 a.m. Pacific on Thursday, Oct. 29, in State Farm Arena. ESPN was first to report the moved time up from the previously-scheduled 8 p.m. Eastern/5 p.m. Pacific time slot, with the WNBA making its official announcement a few minutes later. The news comes two full days after the Valkyries won Game 4 over the Dream, tying the best-of-seven series at two games each and guaranteeing Game 6 would happen. The WNBA did not have an announcement set at the time and, according to multiple reports , had spent the better part of the last two days trying to find a workable solution. In case you have missed it, the Dream have called Gateway Center Arena in College Park home for the last six seasons, which only has a capacity of around 3,500. But the Dream have moved every playoff game this year to the much larger State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta, an arena operated by the NBA's Hawks that holds a little more than 17,000. Ever since the Dream clinched a spot in the WNBA Finals on Oct. 9, it wasn't clear where the league was going to hold the three games in Atlanta. The WNBA set the Finals schedule months in advance with national television partners, and State Farm Arena had conflicts for the dates of Games 3, 4 and 6. But on Oct. 13 , the WNBA announced that Games 3 and 4 would be moved in order to get them played in State Farm Arena. That announcement, though, didn't touch on Game 6 and the league did not answer an SFGATE inquiry at the time about what would happen for a possible Game 6. As of last Friday - as in one day before Game 4 - Hawks chief operating officer Steve Koonin was telling Atlanta sports radio station 92.9 The Game that people should "write your local congressman" if they were trying to help get the game into State Farm Arena and that playing in Gateway Center Arena "might be unavoidable." All of the negotiations sure give the impression that the WNBA avoided coming to a solution because the series might have ended prior to Game 6. According to an ESPN story on Sunday, several sources around the situation "expressed frustration that these issues hadn't been resolved before Saturday." But even with this feasible solution finalized, there's no underscoring just how embarrassing it is for the WNBA to have the arena issues in the middle of the Finals. item.title: Van Dijk on Araujo Liverpool Impact: “Aggressive in the Right Moments”
item.description: After the disappointment of 2025-26, if Liverpool were to turn it around in 2026-27 it was likely always going to come with at least a few storylines or redemption and rediscovery. Nobody, though, would have imagined those stories would include a defender signed on loan from Barcelona. That defender is, of course, Ronald Araujo. The 27-year-old Uruguayan international became an unexpected loan signing when it was made clear to him he didn’t have a future under Hansi Flick with the Catalan giants, and on the back of a few difficult years he jumped at the opportunity for a change of scenery and took a pay cut to join the Reds. His loan deal included a €55M (£47M) purchase option, and if you were a betting man at the moment you’d say it’s a near certainty the club will trigger it and bring Araujo into the fold long-term such has been his impact, which captain Virgil van Dijk was asked about on Sunday. “I think he was very aggressive in the right moments,” Van Dijk said following Liverpool’s 2-0 win over Brighton when asked about the sudden Anfield cult hero. “That’s what we need. You see it with the crowd, the crowd loves it, and that energy can feed the team. “As a team we welcomed him with open arms, we can see his defensive qualities, his presence, and his positive attitude. He doesn’t speak much English but he’s working on it. It is down to him to just keep going now, but it’s great to have him in the team and I think the fans appreciate it as well.” There’s no doubt the fans do appreciate it—or that when Anfield gets fired up feeding off Araujo’s energy it does then help to energize the rest of the team. Which isn’t to say Araujo has been perfect. He hasn’t been far off it, though. And between setting a very high standard mostly at right back but occasionally also at centre half along with never, ever seeming to give less than 100% when he’s on the pitch, it’s easy to see exactly why the crowd already loves him so much. “I think his quality is clear to see,” Van Dijk added. “I think he slots in very well for our back four, he’s a great character, and we’re happy to have him.”

item.title: Texas complained to SEC about refs screwing them vs. Ole Miss
item.description: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Texas complained to SEC about refs screwing them vs. Ole Miss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Texas survived against Ole Miss on Saturday, winning 34-27. The Longhorns had a dominant first half, leading 24-3, but the second half was a different story. Ole Miss tied the game in the fourth. Texas rebuilt a ten-point lead, but Ole Miss knocked it down to a touchdown. They then recovered an onside kick, but Texas was able to keep Ole Miss out of the end zone to win the game . Much of the comeback for Ole Miss was aided by poor play from Texas, including multiple failures on third. Some of those third-down failures were a result of penalties that maybe should not have been called on Texas, and Steve Sarkisian took exception to them after the game, per Tyler Horka of Inside Texas. “Steve Sarkisian says Texas has not gotten feedback from the SEC on some questionable false start calls that went against the Longhorns vs. Ole Miss,” Horka posted on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Texas went three of 13 on third downs and converted just one third down in the second half. Meanwhile, the Longhorns had three false-start penalties in the game, with all three coming on third downs. Also on all three of them, it seemed Ole Miss had jumped into the neutral zone, leading to a member of the Texas offense jumping. Steve Sarkisian says Texas has not gotten feedback from the SEC on some questionable false start calls that went against the Longhorns vs. Ole Miss. This was an example. pic.twitter.com/D3TZAUeCN9 — Tyler Horka (@tbhorka) October 26, 2026 Those should be encroachment calls, but instead they were called as false starts. The only third down of the second half that Texas converted was initially a third-and-six play, but they finally picked up the encroachment flag. That was on a third-and-six that became a third-and-one. The Longhorns converted, but on the next play, Arch Manning was stripped during a sack, and it was recovered for an Ole Miss touchdown. Texas made a massive jump up the polls with the win over Ole Miss. They will host Mississippi State on Saturday. item.title: Eddie Howe: Man United face unexpected obstacle in their bid to replace Michael Carrick
item.description: Eddie Howe: Man United face unexpected obstacle in their bid to replace Michael Carrick If Manchester United part ways with Michael Carrick , Eddie Howe is reportedly the man they will likely turn to. For many, the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday was the final nail in the coffin for Carrick’s United project. The Red Devils have now collected only seven points from eight games and sit 16th in the league table, just two points above bottom-placed Sunderland. If the team had been playing well without the results going their way, there might have been an excuse to hope Carrick could still turn things around. However, the results have reflected the performances: United have been horrendous. Players are not “playing like they mean it” and, as Bruno Fernandes clearly hinted, there are even doubts over Carrick’s tactics. His staying in the job would therefore be baffling. Howe likely to replace Carrick If Carrick does go, Howe has been tipped to replace him . The 48-year-old has Premier League experience, a history of turning struggling sides into competitive ones, and a knack for building teams with a clear identity. Beyond that, The Peoples Person has even shared a piece on how he could transform Joshua Zirkzee and get the best out of the Dutch forward. Yet, while Howe being out of work should, for many, make this a straightforward deal, it has emerged that it will not be. Newcastle due payout if Howe joins new club Newcastle United, whom he left in the summer, are due a payout if another club snaps him up, as Chronicle Live explain: “It is expected that a significant payout would be due to Newcastle given that Howe had a number of years left to run on his contract. “Newcastle are believed to be monitoring what happens next with Howe and Man United.” Crucially, this payout clause will show just how keen INEOS are on hiring Howe. We know the Old Trafford chiefs have a habit of avoiding unnecessary or extra costs when they can. item.title: Orlando Brown Jr. silenced Trey Hendrickson. What that means for Bengals
item.description: BALTIMORE − After the Cincinnati Bengals stormed to a 35-13 comeback win against the Baltimore Ravens , Orlando Brown Jr. was asked about his performance in the game. His response was short but telling. "I'm excited to watch the tape," Brown said. Brown had every right to eagerly anticipate savoring his effort in the Oct. 25 victory at M&T Bank Stadium, which was one of his best performances of the year. After Cincinnati's clear and convincing Week 2 victory over the Houston Texans , Brown was singled out for the sacks and hits to which quarterback Joe Burrow was subjected. But in the month since that Sept. 20 game, Burrow said, he's been happy with Brown's play. That was especially true after Brown's efforts in rendering former Bengals NFL sack champion Trey Hendrickson a near-non factor in the win against the Ravens. "Yes, Orlando is who he is, week in and week out," Burrow said. "We talked about what happened in the one game (at Houston), but really, I think he's been lights-out all year and continues to work really hard to keep getting better and, like you said, I think he played great today." Hendrickson not only didn't sack Burrow but also didn't record a single tackle. Brown and Hendrickson were matched up head-to-head the entire game. Brown played 53 snaps and, according to Pro Football Focus, was the highest-graded Bengals offensive lineman with a 71.9 valuation. Hendrickson's only counting stats in his first game against the Bengals since leaving the organization were quarterback hits, and he had two. Hendrickson might not be in his prime at age 31, plus the Oct. 25 game was his first since missing two games for surgery on his right hand. On the other hand, Hendrickson remains potent. He has two sacks so far in 2026 after the Ravens signed him this past offseason to a four-year, $112 million contract. He also missed 10 games for the Bengals last season due to injury, but his four sacks in 2025 made him one of the team's top pass rushers. "I've got a lot of respect for how (Hendrickson) plays, how he executes," Brown said. "He's one of the best in the world at what he does. We had a great plan as a team and an offense. We were able to go out here and play physical and violent." This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Orlando Brown Jr. silenced Trey Hendrickson. What that means for Bengals

item.title: Ballon d’Or chaos as Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe published as winners on website
item.description: The Ballon d’Or has been plunged into chaos after its official website published three separate articles claiming Harry Kane , Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe had all won the prestigious individual award before the start of the ceremony . The world’s best player of 2026 will be crowned tonight at the London Palladium with Bayern Munich and England striker Kane the favourite , off the back of 89 goals for club and country in just 81 appearances since the start of last season. Follow the Ballon d’Or 2026 LIVE! But in a seemingly colossal error by organisers, Kane was one of three winners promoted by the award’s official website hours before proceedings got underway, with Barcelona sensation Yamal and Real Madrid striker Mbappe - the two other frontrunners - getting similar articles posted. The articles have since been taken down by the website. Harry Kane was one of three to be claimed the Ballon d'Or winner in articles published before the ceremony (Ballon d'Or) Kane’s article was headlined: “Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season”, which went on to examine his “prolific haul” and records that “ensured Bayern won a domestic treble”. Mbappe’s piece claimed he was awarded the Ballon d’Or for “consistency personified at the very highest level” in the headline, following a “record-breaking World Cup and another welter of goals for Los Blancos”. World Cup winner Yamal, meanwhile, had his article led on the 19-year-old’s “unprecedented record ... that not even Lionel Messi managed to achieve”. Branding him the “new king of football”, it continued: 'In fact, at just 19 years of age, Lamine Yamal has just become the youngest winner in the history of the Ballon d'Or, which was established in 1956. Kylian Mbappe also received an article promoting him as the award winner (Ballon d'Or) A similar article was posted for Lamine Yamal (Ballon d'Or) “To truly appreciate the scale of his achievement, one need only recall that not even Lionel Messi – the record holder for the most trophies – had managed to win the Ballon d'Or at that age. “The Argentine star won it for the first time in 2009, when he was 22 years and 160 days old. “The all-time record for the youngest winner, until this magical evening in London, belonged to Ronaldo Nazário, who won the Ballon d'Or at the age of 21 years and 92 days. “Now, this historic record belongs to the new king of football and the brand-new winner of the most prestigious trophy on the planet. “It belongs to Lamine Yamal Nasraoui Ebana.” The ceremony gets underway at 8pm GMT with the Ballon d’Or winner set to be crowned around 9:45pm GMT.

item.title: Jalen Hurts situation creates new problem for Eagles as NFL reportedly grows ‘furious’
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles are facing growing scrutiny over their handling of Jalen Hurts ‘ medical situation, with the NFL reportedly furious about the team’s public messaging. According to Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio , league officials reportedly have no issue with how Philadelphia handled Hurts’ initial treatment in London. However, the team’s response to the controversy has frustrated league executives. Marcus Hayes of The Philadelphia Inquirer reported that a longtime source connected to NFL offices described the league’s officials, saying, “ they’re furious ” with Philadelphia’s communication. item.title: Another major champion quits LIV Golf ahead of proposed relaunch
item.description: Graeme McDowell has become the latest golfer to rule himself out of LIV Golf 's relaunched league. The former US Open champion, 47, from Northern Ireland, joined LIV Golf in 2022. He played for multiple teams in the breakaway circuit, most recently OKGC in 2026, but has now decided to walk away. "I've decided not to pursue LIV 2.0," McDowell confirmed in an X post on Monday. "I'm grateful for the opportunity I've had over the last four years and want to thank everyone who has been part of that journey. I look forward to the next chapter in my career." McDowell's major title came at the 2010 US Open at Pebble Beach. He also won 11 events on the European tour and four on the PGA Tour. His defection follows a string of announced departures. Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton and Tom McKibbin said on Friday that they will not return to LIV in 2027. Jon Rahm will not be a part of LIV 2.0 (PA) Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia, David Puig, Abraham Ancer, Charles Howell III, Adrian Meronk, Louis Oosthuizen and Thomas Pieters are also part of the exodus. The league's financial backdrop has shifted after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced earlier this year that it would end its financial support of LIV Golf. LIV Golf is currently going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. CEO Scott O'Neil has lined up funding for LIV 2.0 as the league goes through those proceedings. Earlier this month, Rory McIlroy declared that LIV Golf is no longer a threat to the traditional game ahead of the proposed relaunch. “LIV had probably like, half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly,” McIlroy told the Bloomberg New Economy forum in New Delhi. “They had a lot of capital but I think a lot of that capital was wasted in some ways and I think they could have used that money a lot more strategically and could have partnered with some of the governing bodies of the game and certainly could have done better things with it instead of just enriching tour pros who were already making a lot of money. “BC Partners have come in and seen an opportunity (but) it looks like every day that goes by there’s another player that was on LIV who is not going to join LIV 2.0 so I think it is going to be very difficult to get out of this Chapter 11 bankruptcy and go forward. “But if they do it is certainly not going to be a threat to the traditional order of the game as it once was.”

item.title: Why UCF football is sticking with Keyone Jenkins as starting QB vs. Baylor
item.description: ORLANDO — UCF football coach Scott Frost will ride the "hot hand" and keep Keyone Jenkins at quarterback for Friday's upcoming Big 12 battle against Baylor . Frost declared Jenkins, a 6-foot, 200-pound senior, the starter with Alonza Barnett III (hamstring) still not fully healthy. Barnett, who started the Knights ' first two games against Bethune-Cookman and Pittsburgh , was available in an emergency capacity this past weekend after being considered a game-time decision. "I'm really pleased with Alonza's progress. I think he probably could play," Frost said. "I don't know if he's 100% yet. "I think the reps have really helped Keyone. He played a pretty special game Saturday and made plays when we needed to make them. I thought the first play in overtime (a 25-yard touchdown pass to Josh Derry ) was elite, him getting out there and finding Josh. He's just capitalized on his opportunity and used the reps that he's gotten in the game to keep playing better and better." Jenkins improved to 3-2 as the Knights' starter with his best performance to date against BYU , the nation's No. 2 team. He completed 25 of 41 attempts for 293 yards and three touchdowns, rushed for another score and, crucially, did not commit a turnover as UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) picked up its first win against an AP top-five opponent in program history. Following the win, Jenkins acknowledged he would likely return to the second-string role once Barnett is available. His week-over-week improvements, however, have given Frost and his staff confidence to leave him as the team's QB1. "It's really up to the coaches, for real. They're going to do what they feel is best for the team," Jenkins said Saturday. "It's really out of my control. item.title: Liverpool force club into major decision, they were ready to pounce
item.description: Liverpool force club into major decision, they were ready to pounce Liverpool have cast their net far and wide for new players over the last couple of years. In fact, over £600 million has been spent by the Anfield outfit on trying to improve their ranks and, while they've managed to do this with some players, others haven't quite hit the mark. Even if every single player was performing to a high standard, there would always be ways to improve. At the moment, it's clear that there are several problem positions among Liverpool's ranks that need to be bolstered. And, even with the transfer window closed, the links haven't slowed down with new players being linked with an Anfield switch on a weekly basis. No concrete deals have come to fruition yet but, the fact that Liverpool are being linked with so many players is definitely a good sign. Liverpool were ready to activate David Otorbi's release clause which forced Valencia into extending his contract One position that Liverpool didn't manage to strengthen in the summer was right-wing. Mohamed Salah exited and, from that point on, everyone thought that a new right-winger would be on top of Liverpool's priority list. Evidently, that wasn't the case and, although Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola were brought in , neither of them are natural right-wingers. Both players can be used there if needed but, in reality, everyone knows that the Reds would've been better off signing a proepr right-winger. Attempts to sign one were made by Liverpool but, nothing ever came of it. However, as per a fresh update from Tribuna Deportiva, Julian Ward was about to change that and activate the release clause of Valencia right-winger, David Otorbi. "Liverpool informed VCF and the player’s entourage this week that they wanted to PAY THE CLAUSE of David Otrobi of 30M," they wrote . Liverpool could have got their hands on an elite talent in David Otorbi Otorbi probably isn't a player that many Liverpool fans will have heard of. The 19-year-old currently plays for Valencia and has been a regular feature in their team since the start of the 2026-27 season. Statistically, his numbers aren't the most impressive with the attacker only scoring one goal this term. But, the fact that he's a natural right winger who can also be used as a left-winger or a striker is massively beneficial. He's also only 19 years old so, even though he's already a fairly impressive player, there's plenty of room for him to grow into an even better one. For the €30 million that Liverpool wanted him for, Otorbi would have been an absolute steal but, now Valencia are likely to extend his contract and bump his release clause up to €60 million, the deal doesn't really represent good value anymore. However, it does show that the Reds are still on the lookout for a new right-winger, which should be music to the ears of fans.
